memory_candidates.content: When converting a formerly-unconditional blocking predicate into an evidence-gated one that must still surface the suppressed case loudly, materialize the candidate overlap list ONCE and derive both selections from it rather than re-scanning. In orchestrate-batch-admit.sh: build $overlaps (full annotated overlap list with an in_flight discriminator key on each element), then $hit = first blocking member (map(select(scope==in_batch or in_flight)) | first) and $idle_overlap = first suppressed member (map(select(scope==cross_batch and not in_flight)) | first). Both preserve the original first-match/ascending-project_number determinism, the comprehension body stays a verbatim copy so the untouched disjunct (in_batch) is bit-for-bit unaffected, and no second invocation of the overlap predicate is needed. Factor the always-optional appended field into one `$idle_advisory_frag` variable computed once, appended via `+` to every verdict branch that needs it, rather than repeating an if/else three times.

A test suite's own negative control for a new regression case is not optional theater: when adding a positive test for a bug fix, temporarily swap the working file for its pre-fix git blob (e.g. `git show <pre-fix-sha>:path > path`, run the suite, then restore from a scratch backup copy -- never git reset --hard on a dirty tree), confirm the NEW case specifically fails, then restore and re-verify green. A new test that would have passed against the old, buggy code is not testing the fix at all -- it is only testing that the fixture parses. This caught nothing wrong in this task's case, but the negative-control run is what actually proves the two new admission-predicate test cases (predicate 2.5, four-tier 12) exercise the v5 narrowing rather than merely re-asserting pre-existing behavior.
